Limbs follow reconstruction proportions, not fossil-measured lengths."},"anatomy":["Broad, oval abdomen widest anterior-middle and rounded posterior, attached broadly to triangular/subtriangular carapace with pointed anterior apex. No narrow spider pedicel.","Raised broad anterior abdominal tergite2–3 as labeled in source, then transverse abdominal plates with median and lateral subdivisions; terminal dorsal plate9 broad and undivided. Do not copy Trigonotarbus separate2/3 or pear-shaped posterior taper blindly.","Four pairs of articulated walking legs, two pairs directed anterior/outward and two lateral/posterior; long enough to match whole-animal drawing, not stumpy invented legs. Central anterior pair in reconstruction are palps, not fifth walking pair or antennae.","Small anterior mouthparts conservative beneath head; eyes only restrained low relief consistent with reconstruction, not large spider-like bulbous eyes.","No exposed external tail, spinnerets, wings, scorpion pincers or spiny armor. Ventral pygidium is not a tail. Fine setae/ornament may be omitted at lowpoly scale."],"restoration_boundaries":["Actual carbonized holotype photo in2022Fig1D viewed; correct panelD only, not neighboring myriapodE. Real photo confirms body silhouette; reconstructed limbs supply missing functional anatomy.","Palaeotarbus is replacement name for Eotarbus jerami; do not confuse with the earlier Carboniferous taxon bearing Eotarbus name.","The original rounded abdomen and headshield gate is retained; limb stoutness must follow actual published reconstruction rather than exaggeration.","Body depth/color/pose inferred. No claim this is a scan or exact preserved whole animal."]}
